chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥabīb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who had dinars with me and who was ill. He said to me, “If something happens to me, then give so-and-so twenty dinars, and give my sister the remainder of the dinars.” Then he died, and I did not witness his death. Then a truthful Muslim man came to me and said, “He instructed me to tell you: Look to the dinars which I ordered you to pay to my sister, and give ten dinars from them in charity; distribute them among the Muslims.” And his sister did not know that I had anything with me.
So he عليه السلام said: “I view that you should give ten dinars from it in charity, as he said.”

key_terms.أُخْتِي: my sister, the designated recipient of the remainder
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the Muslims among whom the charity is to be distributed
key_terms.بِعَشَرَةِ دَنَانِيرَ: with ten dinars, the specified charitable amount
key_terms.دَنَانِيرُ: gold dinars that had been entrusted for safekeeping
key_terms.صَادِقٌ: truthful, describing the Muslim messenger conveying the instruction
key_terms.فَتَصَدَّقْ: give in charity from the wealth
key_terms.مَرِيضًا: ill, indicating the context of a death-related instruction

ai.seo_question: If a deceased person’s later instruction about charity is conveyed by a truthful Muslim, should it be carried out from the entrusted dinars?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a case of bequest involving deposited wealth, a later verbal instruction, and the distribution of part of the property as charity. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام rules that the ten dinars should be given in charity according to the deceased man’s instruction.
